question: A student walks at a speed of 5 km/h. When he increases his speed to 6 km/h, he reaches school 20 minutes earlier. Find the distance covered by the student.
solution:
Given:

Normal speed of the student = 5 km/h.

Increased speed = 6 km/h

Time = 20 Minutes less

**Formula:**

D = S × T, where

D = Distance covered

S = Speed

T = Time 

Calculations:

Let the Distance be "D"

According to the question-

⇒ Time taken under normal speed = Dover5 hr

⇒ Time taken under increased speed = Dover6 hr

It is given that - 

⇒ Dover5 - Dover6 = 20over60

⇒ D(6-5over30) = 1over3 

Solving for D, we get D = 10 km

∴ The distance covered by the student is 10 km.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**Distance = (product of speed )/(difference of speed)× difference of time[time in hr]

Distance = (6 × 5)/(1)× (20)/(60) = 2 × 5 = 10 km
